faenĕrātĭo (less correctly fēn-, foen- ), ōnis, f. id.,
I.a lending on interest, usury (class.): “haec pecunia tota ab honoribus translata est in quaestum et faenerationem,” Cic. Fl. 23, 56 : “nec enim, si tuam ob causam cuiquam commodes, beneficium illud habendum est, sed faeneratio,” id. Fin. 2, 35, 117 ; id. Verr. 2, 3, 72, § 168; Col. 1 praef. § 8.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
